name: Melius
product: Agent-driven creative canvas that generates ad campaigns, images, video and audio from plain-language prompts across many AI models.
pricing_model: Subscription; third-party listings report paid plans from about $17/month billed yearly
round_stage: Series A (announced together with earlier seed)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Nigerian, Kenyan and South African SMEs and freelance social media managers could pay a low monthly plan to produce ad creatives and short videos for Instagram, TikTok and Facebook campaigns without hiring designers.
founders: Joowon Kim, Young Kim, Arnav Ramu
notes: Founders are ex-Ramp engineers; TechCrunch reports >$1M annualized revenue within two months of leaving stealth in July 2026. Low entry price suits card-free subscription payments.

name: fonio.ai
product: AI voice and omnichannel agents that answer and handle customer calls and messages for small and medium-sized businesses.
expansion_signal: Funding is meant to put AI customer-communication tools in the hands of SMBs across Europe and the United States; company later reported passing $10M ARR.
africa_use_case: Clinics, salons, restaurants and property agents in Lagos, Nairobi or Accra that miss calls could pay for an AI receptionist that answers, books and follows up in English or French.
notes: $140M post-money valuation. Site already localised in several languages (FR/NL/ES pages seen), which helps francophone Africa.

name: Respond.io
product: Customer conversation platform that unifies WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, calls and other channels with AI agents for B2C sales and support teams.
pricing_model: Subscription by monthly active contacts: Starter $79/month yearly ($99 monthly), Growth $159-$199/month, Advanced and Enterprise higher
expansion_signal: Raise is earmarked to scale into North America and Europe, and TechCrunch reports the company is eyeing acquisitions in those regions.
africa_use_case: African e-commerce sellers, schools and fintech support teams that already sell and serve customers over WhatsApp could pay for a shared inbox with AI agents.
notes: Endeavor Catalyst participated. Starter tier sits at the top of the target price band; Growth tier is slightly above it.

name: Lovable
product: AI software creation platform that builds websites, web apps and online businesses from plain-language prompts.
pricing_model: Freemium: Free tier, Pro $25/month, Business $50/month, Enterprise custom (credit-based)
lead_investors: Menlo Ventures; Scaleup Europe Fund (managed by EQT)
expansion_signal: Funding will expand the platform, infrastructure and global team.
africa_use_case: African solo founders, agencies and small businesses could pay $25/month to build storefronts, booking sites and internal tools without hiring developers, which is a large unmet need across the continent.
notes: $13.3B valuation. Recurring card-billed subscriptions are a direct fit for Cozzipay auto-renewal.

name: Wassist
product: No-code platform that gives Shopify brands an AI agent selling and answering order questions inside WhatsApp.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: WhatsApp is the main shopping channel for many African online sellers, so fashion, beauty and electronics merchants in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana could pay to automate sales chats and order tracking there.
notes: Meta Business Partner per Seedtable. Preqin dates the round June 2, 2026; press coverage appeared June 8, 2026.

name: Tano
product: Creator advertising platform where AI agents and human strategists find creators, negotiate, seed products and pay creators for brand campaigns.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Consumer brands and app companies selling into Africa could use Tano to run campaigns with African TikTok and Instagram creators.
notes: Clients cited include Unilever and HelloFresh; this is a brand-side, partly managed service rather than self-serve, so Cozzipay fit is weak.

name: Numina
product: Free AI-powered bookkeeping platform where small businesses issue invoices, connect bank accounts and file VAT returns.
pricing_model: Free core platform; monetisation model Not found
lead_investors: Not found (investors: Founders A/S, Emblem, Nebular, The Nordic Web, angels)
expansion_signal: Capital will adapt the free accounting platform for small businesses across Europe beyond Denmark.
africa_use_case: Freelancers and micro-businesses in Africa who need simple invoicing and bookkeeping could adopt a free AI ledger if it is localised for local tax rules.
founders: Jakob Olund Kristensen, Simon Boel Have
notes: Domain taken from Trustpilot and the company's GitHub MCP server address (api.numina.app). Free product and Denmark-specific VAT focus limit near-term payment volume.

name: Holo
product: AI marketing autopilot that reads a business's website and then plans, writes and publishes its ads, social posts, emails and SEO content.
pricing_model: Credit-based subscription; third-party reviews cite roughly $20-$48/month
expansion_signal: None stated (funds go to product development, reaching more small businesses and growing the Vilnius team)
africa_use_case: African SMEs that cannot afford an agency could pay about $20/month for always-on social posts, ads and email campaigns generated from their website.
notes: Third-party review cites ~1,095 Trustpilot reviews, which points to a large self-serve base. Price point fits the target band well.

name: Zeliq
product: AI sales workspace combining prospecting data, enrichment, outreach and AI sales agents in one interface.
expansion_signal: Funding is meant to advance its AI sales agents and expand market reach.
africa_use_case: B2B startups and outsourcing firms in Lagos, Nairobi, Casablanca or Dakar selling abroad could pay per seat for prospect data and automated outreach, with French support for francophone markets.
founders: Dorian Ciavarella, Victor Lennel, Guillaume Cruz
notes: Total funding about €21M. Dealroom describes the target as mid-market sales teams, so self-serve SMB pricing is unconfirmed.

name: Passionfroot
product: Platform and marketplace that lets B2B creators (newsletters, podcasts, LinkedIn voices) package, sell and manage sponsorships with brands.
expansion_signal: Expanding the marketplace into the US with a New York office, and into Brazil.
africa_use_case: African tech and business newsletter writers and podcasters could use it to sell sponsorships, and African B2B startups could buy creator placements to reach local audiences.
notes: Brazil expansion shows appetite for emerging markets; good opening for an Africa pitch.

name: Clueso
product: Agentic video platform that turns prompts, documents, decks or screen recordings into finished product, training and marketing videos with AI voiceover and captions.
pricing_model: Freemium; tiered plans from solo creators to enterprise (amounts not confirmed)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African SaaS startups, online course creators and training firms could pay monthly to produce product demos and tutorial videos without studios or voice talent.
founders: Akash Anand, Neel Balar, Prajwal Prakash
notes: YC-backed; more than 1,000 companies use it per the press release.

name: Revora (formerly MyAlice)
product: AI commerce agents that recommend products, recover carts and complete purchases inside WhatsApp, Instagram and branded storefronts in the shopper's dialect.
expansion_signal: Proceeds go mainly to growth in Saudi Arabia, its largest market; another write-up describes ambitions across 21+ countries.
africa_status: No visible Africa presence (investor list per Preqin includes Flat6Labs; no African market named)
africa_use_case: Arabic-first conversational commerce suits Egyptian, Moroccan and Sudanese online merchants who sell over WhatsApp and Instagram.
notes: Also supports in-chat payments, so position Cozzipay as a payment method inside its flows rather than a competitor. Check whether its 21+ countries include North Africa.

name: Sowilo (Catecut)
product: Catecut reads fashion product photos and writes SEO-ready titles, descriptions, tags, metadata and alt text, delivered as a Shopify app.
lead_investors: Kría fund (per Inforcapital); TGC Capital and angels participated
expansion_signal: Funding supports the global rollout of its Shopify app and international growth across key retail markets.
africa_use_case: African fashion and jewellery brands selling on Shopify could automate multilingual product listings for export.
notes: Sold through the Shopify App Store, which bills merchants by card. Small team; amount not disclosed.

name: Keep Converting
hq_country: United States (Los Angeles per press release; some outlets describe it as UAE-based)
product: AI conversion platform that generates a personalised product-page experience for each e-commerce visitor in real time.
expansion_signal: Reports active client deployments in the United States, Europe and the Gulf.
africa_use_case: Mid-sized African DTC brands with real traffic could pay to lift conversion on product pages.
notes: HQ reporting conflicts (LA vs UAE). Unclear whether the product is self-serve or deployed per client.

name: Broccoli AI
product: AI customer service and scheduling agents that answer calls and book jobs for plumbers, electricians, HVAC and other home-service businesses.
round_stage: Series A and Series B (announced together)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Growing plumbing, solar-install and appliance-repair firms in South Africa or Kenya could use an AI front desk to capture and schedule jobs.
notes: YC-backed. Deep integrations with US home-service software make an Africa launch less likely in the near term.

name: Runable
product: AI agent platform that builds websites, slide decks and other assets, and is extending into helping small businesses find customers and grow.
lead_investors: Susquehanna Venture Capital; Nexus Venture Partners
expansion_signal: None stated (expansion is into growth and marketing features rather than new geographies)
africa_use_case: African small-business owners and freelancers could use one AI agent to build a website, pitch deck and marketing assets for a modest subscription.
founders: Saksham Sarda and co-founder Kumar (full name not confirmed in sources seen)
notes: A pricing analysis (useautumn.com) cites about 1.7 million users. An India-built product priced for emerging markets is a good match.

name: Artwod
product: Gamified drawing-lesson and community app for visual artists, now launching a creators' marketplace.
pricing_model: Subscription plans (pricing page exists; amounts not confirmed)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Young aspiring illustrators and comic artists in Africa could pay a small monthly subscription for structured drawing practice and later sell work through the marketplace.
notes: Consumer-creator subscription; site has Portuguese content, which points to openness to localisation.

name: Fluencify
product: AI-run creator and UGC marketing service that matches brands with vetted creators and handles briefs, posting, paid boosting and cross-border payouts.
expansion_signal: Runs campaigns through a global network of vetted creators.
africa_use_case: African fintech, edtech and consumer-app startups could buy short-form creator campaigns, and African creators could join the network for paid work.
founders: Erik Romdhane, Isaac Norin, Sam Stones Hälleberg
notes: Reported passing $2M ARR six months after launch. Customers are mainly consumer apps, AI tools, fintech and DTC brands.

name: Hypefy AI
product: AI platform that automates the execution of influencer marketing campaigns for brands.
expansion_signal: Capital will accelerate international commercial expansion across Europe and the United States and grow a multi-regional team.
africa_use_case: African consumer brands and agencies could automate influencer campaigns across local creators instead of managing them by hand.
notes: Follows a $1.75M seed in 2025.

name: Noise
hq_country: United States (city not confirmed; founders met at St. Louis startup Answers)
product: App where everyday people earn per view for branded videos they post, while brands set their own CPM and budget with no contracts.
pricing_model: Usage-based: brands pay per view at a self-set CPM; no upfront payment
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African SMEs and apps could pay small per-view budgets for authentic local creator content, and the creator side could tap Africa's large young TikTok user base.
founders: Diego Kafie (CEO), Stu Feldt, Nic Weber
notes: Reports 1.5M creators. Self-serve brand sign-up in minutes; low minimum spend suits SMBs.

name: Dreamteam
hq_country: United States (San Francisco; engineering in Chennai, India)
product: AI-native CRM that fills itself in from emails, calls and meetings, with AI teammates handling lead research, follow-ups and pipeline monitoring.
pricing_model: $49 per seat/month plus AI credit packs at $30/month
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Lean B2B sales teams at African SaaS, logistics and fintech startups could replace spreadsheets with an affordable self-updating CRM.
founders: Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy, Senthil Kanthaswamy
notes: Ex-Freshworks founders, a team with a track record of selling SMB SaaS into emerging markets. Premji Invest also participated.

name: Dimension (SellerOS)
product: SellerOS, an agentic AI operating system that runs TikTok Shop and other social-commerce operations for sellers and agencies.
lead_investors: Not found (participants: Science Inc., UpscaleX, OpenSky, Long Run Capital, 1864 Fund, Lawrence Hsu, Austin Sprinz)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African sellers and agencies that run social-commerce stores could use it to manage operations if TikTok Shop expands to African markets.
notes: Says it is profitable. Value in Africa depends on TikTok Shop availability there.

name: Merchantee
product: Agentic marketplace-intelligence platform that automates pricing and product promotion for online marketplace sellers using competitor and sales data.
expansion_signal: Expanding into Poland and Germany in 2026, then France, the Netherlands and Italy in 2027, with new marketplace integrations (eMag, Bol, Cdiscount).
africa_use_case: Sellers on African marketplaces such as Jumia or Takealot could use automated repricing and promotion, but this needs new marketplace integrations.
notes: Europe-only marketplace roadmap; Africa would be a later-stage pitch.

name: Affinity Labs
product: Venture studio that co-founds and builds AI-powered software and mobile app brands with content creators, who get equity.
pricing_model: Not found (creator partnership/equity model; consumer apps sold to creators' audiences)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Large African creators in fitness, beauty or finance could co-launch paid subscription apps for their audiences, which would need local payment options to convert fans.
founders: Edoardo Ricci, Ahmed Eltom, Sunny Panchal
notes: Not a self-serve tool; the Cozzipay angle is payments for its consumer apps sold to African fan bases.

name: Ranketta
product: AI-visibility (generative engine optimisation) platform that tracks how e-commerce products appear in ChatGPT, Gemini and other AI answers and fixes product data.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African DTC and e-commerce brands could monitor and improve how AI assistants recommend their products as AI shopping grows.
notes: Separate from its €1M pre-seed in November 2025; TheSaaSNews (Nov 2026) says total funding is now about €2M. Seed lead investor not confirmed.

name: Chatsi
product: Conversational AI sales agent that acts like an expert salesperson in chat on e-commerce stores.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African online electronics, beauty and furniture stores could add an AI sales assistant to answer product questions and raise conversion.
notes: Founded 2024. Amount is a financing commitment rather than a fully closed round.

name: Kopa.ai
product: AI agents that run Google Ads, marketing creative, budgeting and store operations for e-commerce brands.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African e-commerce brands that run Google Ads without an in-house marketer could let AI agents manage campaigns and budgets.
founders: Tomas Kozlovskis, Vytautas Narkevicius, Donatas Benaitis, Vytautas Krutulis
notes: Announced 2026-05-28, three days inside the window.

name: Thermit (Creazy)
product: Creazy, a multi-agent AI that produces high-performing marketing content and product-page materials for online sellers.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African marketplace and social sellers could generate product images and ad copy in minutes instead of paying designers.
founders: Kim Jiseong (CEO, per his GitHub profile)
notes: Early stage and Korea-focused; English-language availability not confirmed.

name: Malachyte
product: Behaviour-intelligence engine that personalises e-commerce recommendations in real time from clicks, hovers and searches, including for first-time visitors.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Larger African online retailers with high anonymous traffic could raise conversion with real-time recommendations.
founders: Sidd Motwani, Ian Anderson, Shivaditya Sinha
notes: Available to Shopify merchants but also serves enterprise retailers; SMB pricing unconfirmed.

name: Rebel Audio
product: AI podcasting platform for recording, editing, clipping, translating, publishing and monetising podcasts.
round_amount_usd: Not disclosed (round targets $10M at ~$50M post-money valuation)
expansion_signal: Press release says HardScope will accelerate its AI technology, creator ecosystem and global expansion.
africa_use_case: Africa's fast-growing podcast scene (Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa) could pay $15-$35/month for all-in-one recording, editing and translation into local languages.
notes: Public beta opened to creators worldwide in June 2026. Domain rebel.audio belongs to an unrelated hardware company, so the website is left as Not found.

name: Higgsfield
hq_country: United States (San Francisco; R&D roots in Kazakhstan)
product: AI video, image and audio generation platform for creators, brands and agencies, including product-URL-to-ad generation.
pricing_model: Credit-based subscriptions with a free plan; e.g. Ultra tier about $99/month billed annually
expansion_signal: Reports more than 30 million users across 238 countries; new funds go to scaling go-to-market toward business customers.
africa_status: No visible Africa presence (company reports users in 238 countries)
africa_use_case: African content creators, musicians and ad agencies already experimenting with AI video could pay monthly plans if they can fund them without a dollar card.
founders: Alex Mashrabov, Yerzat Dulat, Mahi De Silva
notes: $5.4B valuation and ~$700M annualized revenue; Series B later extended with TCV and NVIDIA (Oct 2026). Probably already has African users who are blocked by card payments.

name: Loopia
product: AI agents that handle customer service, sales follow-up and cart recovery for online stores and marketplace sellers.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Portuguese-language support makes it relevant for Angolan and Mozambican online sellers, and the model fits marketplace sellers across Africa.
notes: Reported 25x growth in 2025. Lusophone Africa is a natural first market if it goes abroad.
